findingDetails.title: A document naming returns a mention before a later request clause is read
findingDetails.evidence: COMMAND_AS_DOCUMENT returns true from commandOnlyMentioned on the document noun alone, before the COMMAND_ASKED_BY_PRONOUN check at line 460. "open the /deep:review command file, then run it" reads as a mention and typedCommandForTop returns undefined; attachCommand("system-deep-loop", SINGLE("review"), "read the /deep:review docs, then do a thorough review of this diff") returns undefined although DEPTH_REQUEST matches "thorough". The contract at lines 403-407 says a use-verb clause with "it" turns an earlier naming into a request.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Ran the exported guards and consumer on two concrete prompts; both classify as mentions. The old tree had no document return and the unchanged pronoun regex matches the tail "command file, then run it", so the earlier read was a request. REQUEST6 and CONTROL5 carry no document naming, which is why the suite stays green.
findingDetails.recommendation: Move the COMMAND_AS_DOCUMENT return after the COMMAND_ASKED_BY_PRONOUN check, or let that check win when the clause carries a use verb, and add a row that names the document then asks to run it.

claimAdjudication.claim: The new document rule returns a mention before the existing pronoun-request rule can read a later request, so a prompt that asks to run the command loses it.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the determiner test or the tail split excludes these prompts; neither does. Checked whether the deep-loop depth gate rescues the hub case; it runs after the mention check at line 527.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: A reader naming the command file may be assumed not to want the run. Rejected: both prompts carry an explicit later request and the function comment says that clause wins.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if no caller reaches the guard with a document naming plus a later request, or if the reorder makes both prompts read as requests.

findingDetails.title: A limiting negation after the name reads as a refusal
findingDetails.evidence: COMMAND_DECLINED_BY_PRONOUN ends at "it\b", so a qualifier after "it" still satisfies the refusal. "run /speckit:save and don't run it twice" reads as a mention and typedCommandForTop returns undefined; "run /deep:review but never run it without a budget" does the same on the hub path. spec.md:150 records this class as a High risk with REQUEST6, CONTROL5 and the wrapper matrix as the mitigation; none carries a limiting clause after "it".
findingDetails.scopeProof: Ran the exported guards on both prompts; both classify as mentions and the typed command is dropped. The unchanged lead tests cannot produce this reading: the pre-name decline would need "do not run /speckit:save", and the bare-ask lead is false, so b8ebee37d75 returned a request.
findingDetails.recommendation: Bound the tail refusal to a clause that ends at "it" or continues with a sentence boundary, and add REQUEST6 rows for a limiting clause after "it".

claimAdjudication.claim: The tail refusal matches a negated use verb plus "it" without bounding what follows, so a request that limits how the command runs is read as a refusal and the command is dropped.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Searched the fixtures for a limiting clause after "it": the one negative tail row is "don't skip it", and the negation rows all sit before the name. Checked the "why not" guard at line 367; it does not apply.
claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: "don't run it twice" could be read as refusing a second run, which is still a refusal of a run. Rejected as the intended reading for a clause that limits a run already asked for.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the rule is narrowed to a clause ending at "it" and these prompts then read as requests.

findingDetails.title: A markdown link label abuts its target and the naming stops being an occurrence
findingDetails.evidence: The fold drops brackets and parentheses, so "[/create:readme](https://example.com/docs)" becomes "/create:readmehttps://example.com/docs"; the lookahead at line 451 rejects the name and occurrences.length is 0 at line 452. "do not run [/create:readme](https://example.com/docs) yet" reads as a request and attachCommand returns /create:readme. The wrapper matrix pins "[name]" with nothing after the closing bracket.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Probed the guard and attachCommand with a linked label, a parenthesized aside with no space and the bracketed form the matrix covers; only the merged forms flip to request.
findingDetails.recommendation: Drop the "](target)" pair before the fold, or treat "](" as a boundary so the label keeps its own occurrence.

findingDetails.title: The post-name reader covers one clause shape, so a question or a sibling refusal after the name still reads as a request
findingDetails.evidence: The new rule reads "(do not|don't|dont|never) <use verb> it" after the name while the ask rule at line 460 needs the clause to open with a use verb; COMMAND_ASK_LEADS only matches before the name. "/create:readme, what does it do?" reads as a request and attachCommand offers /create:readme; "/create:readme is wrong, skip it" also reads as a request even though "skip" is a decline lead before the name at line 376.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Probed four post-name shapes (question, skip it, won't run it, no need to run it); all return false and the first two offer the command. The pre-name lists already treat skip and won't as refusals.
findingDetails.recommendation: Read a post-name question clause ("what does it do") and the pre-name decline vocabulary after the name, or record the narrower contract in the comment.
